## **Objectives Map**

***

The following collapsed table shows where specific learning goals can be found in the case study. 

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Objectives Map: Where It Is Covered"}


| Learning Goal          | Explanation / Practice                            | Location                |
| :----------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------|:-----------------------|
| Describe ways in which version control facilitates reproducible science | Learn what reproducibility means and how version control makes analyses more reproducible.| [Introduction to Git and GitHub](https://www.opencasestudies.org/ocs-bio-version-control/#reproducibility-and-version-control) |
| Explain how version control works | Understand how version control works by recording differences between commits. | [Introduction to Git and GitHub](https://www.opencasestudies.org/ocs-bio-version-control/#git) |
| Create and make changes to a repository with Git and GitHub | Create new repositories (both locally with Git and remotely with GitHub) and use Git and GitHub to track the history of an analysis. |[Introduction to Git and GitHub](https://www.opencasestudies.org/ocs-bio-version-control/#getting-started-with-git-and-github), [Data Visualization](https://www.opencasestudies.org/ocs-bio-version-control/#data-visualization), [Data Analysis](https://www.opencasestudies.org/ocs-bio-version-control/#data-analysis) | |
| Open a pull request and request a review | Open a pull request to propose changes to a repository, practice requesting a review from a collaborator. | [Pull Requests](https://www.opencasestudies.org/ocs-bio-version-control/#pull-requests) |
| Organize a repository | Understand best practices in scientific project organization. Add additional files to the repository, following the existing organization structure. | [Scientific Project Organization](https://www.opencasestudies.org/ocs-bio-version-control/#scientific-project-organization), [Data Visualization](https://www.opencasestudies.org/ocs-bio-version-control/#data-visualization) | | 
| Identify the benefits and limitations of meta-analyses | Learn about what meta-analyses are, why they are used, and limitations to combining data from multiple studies. | [Context](https://www.opencasestudies.org/ocs-bio-version-control/#what-is-a-meta-analysis) | 
| Explain why infant gut microbiome studies may be useful | Learn what a microbiome is, the importance of the gut microbiome to human health, and why infancy is a useful time to study the gut microbiome. | [Context](https://www.opencasestudies.org/ocs-bio-version-control/#what-is-a-microbiome) |
| Create visualizations to compare sampling designs | Create plots to compare the sampling designs of the original studies used in the meta-analysis described in this case study. |[Data Visualization](https://www.opencasestudies.org/ocs-bio-version-control/#data-visualization)|


:::
